name: impyramid_expand
expr: y = impyramid(I, 'expand'); ysize = size(y); yint = y(2:end-1, 2:end-1); ysum_int = sum(yint(:)); yctr = y(round(end/2), round(end/2));
comment: Sig: B = impyramid(A, 'expand'). Output: (2M-1)x(2N-1). KNOWN GAP: numkit uses literal Burt-Adelson zero-stuff + [1 4 6 4 1]/16 kernel (matches Octave-image bit-equal); MATLAB R2025b uses imresize-with-piecewise-constant-kernel (kernel handle defined inline in toolbox/images/images/impyramid.m). Interior values agree bit-equal across all three engines; only boundary samples differ. Spec pins (a) output shape and (b) interior sum + center value to catch real regressions while tolerating the boundary-handling divergence. Full bit-equal with MATLAB requires either custom-kernel support in imresize or a rewrite of impyramid to inline the imresize math (~150 LOC, deferred).
